summary.text: A 67-year-old man with ESRD on hemodialysis, hypertension, COPD and prior GI bleeds presented to an outside hospital with shortness of breath and hemoptysis. Serology showed positive p-ANCA (1:80), anti-MPO and anti-DNase antibodies with no pulmonary cavities or nodules; granulomatosis with polyangiitis was considered, and he was switched from hydralazine 100 mg three times daily to nifedipine and discharged after IV antibiotics.

He was readmitted for potential sepsis and skin lesions with purpuric papules, plaques and nodules, treated initially as disseminated herpes zoster with valacyclovir, had negative lumbar puncture and serologic workup, and was switched to doxycycline and prednisone. Dermatology follow-up two months later found no active lesions and a biopsy showing a reparative reaction.

Months later he was readmitted for suspected pneumonia and an active GI bleed with hemoglobin 30 g/L and bilateral infiltrates, received IV vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam, and was transferred. Hydralazine was inadvertently restarted, and within 24 hours he developed violaceous bullae, purpuric nodules and plaques, facial edema and fever, followed during the hospitalization by metabolic encephalopathy, sepsis and acute hypoxic failure.

Skin biopsy showed a subepidermal blister, epidermal necrosis, neutrophilic infiltrate and ovoid structures resembling Cryptococcus with negative GMS and DCAS stains, and vasculitis was noted on biopsy, supporting cryptococcoid Sweet syndrome with hydralazine-induced ANCA vasculitis. Hydralazine was stopped and high-dose corticosteroids given with rapid improvement, and hydralazine was added to the allergy list.
